dmTitle.infoName: System Architecture, Interfaces, and Data Flows

levelledPara.title: Introduction
levelledPara.para: This data module describes the detailed architecture, component layout, interface definitions, and data flow paths for the AMPEL360 Q100 Indicating and Recording System (ATA 31). The system employs a distributed, networked architecture leveraging Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) principles and multiple data bus standards.

levelledPara.title: Functional Architecture
levelledPara.para: The Indicating and Recording System is organized into five primary functional domains:

1. Display Management - Controls all cockpit displays and rendering
2. Crew Alerting - Processes and presents warnings, cautions, and advisories
3. Data Acquisition - Collects parameters from aircraft sensors and systems
4. Data Recording - Stores flight data in crash-protected and maintenance recorders
5. System Hosting - Provides computational resources via IMA modules

levelledPara.title: Physical Architecture
levelledPara.para: Major line-replaceable units (LRUs) and their installation locations:

- Display Units (4x): Cockpit instrument panel (2 PFD, 2 ND/MFD)
- Display Management Computer (2x): Avionics bay (redundant)
- Crew Alerting Computer (2x): Avionics bay (redundant)
- Data Acquisition Units (4x): Distributed locations for sensor proximity
- Flight Data Recorder (1x): Aft pressure bulkhead (crash-protected)
- Cockpit Voice Recorder (1x): Aft pressure bulkhead (crash-protected)
- Quick Access Recorder (1x): Forward electronics bay
- ACMS Gateway (2x): Avionics bay (redundant)
- IMA Cabinets (4x): Avionics bay (provides hosting for applications)

levelledPara.title: AFDX (ARINC 664) Network
levelledPara.para: Primary high-speed data network for system-to-system communication. Configuration:

- Dual redundant switched Ethernet networks (A and B)
- 100 Mbps full-duplex per end system
- Deterministic traffic shaping via Virtual Links (VLs)
- Used for: Display data, alert messages, FMS data, navigation data
- Segregation: Flight-critical traffic on separate VLs from non-critical

levelledPara.title: ARINC 429 Buses
levelledPara.para: Point-to-point digital data buses for sensor interfaces and legacy system integration:

- Approximately 60 ARINC 429 buses throughout the aircraft
- Data rates: High-speed (100 kbps) and low-speed (12.5 kbps)
- Used for: Air data, inertial reference, GPS, discrete signals
- Routed through Data Acquisition Units for aggregation to AFDX

levelledPara.title: Discrete and Analog Interfaces
levelledPara.para: Direct wired connections for time-critical or simple signals:

- Discrete inputs: Switch positions, circuit breaker status, landing gear position
- Analog inputs: Temperature probes, pressure transducers, flow sensors
- Analog-to-digital conversion performed at Data Acquisition Units
- Signal conditioning: Filtering, scaling, fault detection

levelledPara.title: MIL-STD-1553 Buses
levelledPara.para: Dual redundant buses for flight-critical systems requiring deterministic timing:

- Used for: Flight control computers, air data computers, inertial reference
- 1 Mbps data rate
- Bus controller hosted on primary flight control computer
- Remote terminals at indicating and recording interfaces

levelledPara.title: Cross-ATA System Interfaces
levelledPara.para: The Indicating and Recording System interfaces with the following aircraft systems:

ATA 21 (Environmental Control):
- Cabin pressure, temperature, humidity sensors
- ECS fault alerts and system status
ATA 22 (Auto Flight):
- Autopilot engagement status and modes
- Flight director commands and deviations
- Autothrottle status
ATA 24 (Electrical Power):
- Bus voltages, currents, frequencies
- Generator status, battery state-of-charge
- Circuit breaker trip indications
ATA 27 (Flight Controls):
- Control surface positions
- Actuator pressures and temperatures
- Flight control computer status
ATA 29 (Hydraulic Power):
- System pressures, reservoir levels
- Pump status and temperatures
ATA 32 (Landing Gear):
- Gear position (up/down/transit)
- Brake temperatures and pressures
- Tire pressure monitoring
ATA 34 (Navigation):
- GPS position, altitude, groundspeed
- Inertial reference data
- Radio navigation signal quality
ATA 42 (IMA):
- Computational hosting for display and alert applications
- AFDX switching and routing
- Partitioned execution environments
ATA 45 (Maintenance System):
- BITE results from all LRUs
- Fault codes and maintenance messages
- Trend data for predictive maintenance
ATA 71-80 (Propulsion):
- Fuel cell stack voltages, currents, temperatures
- Electric motor speeds, torques, temperatures
- Hydrogen pressure and flow
- Battery pack state-of-charge and cell voltages

levelledPara.title: External Interfaces
levelledPara.para: Connections to systems outside the aircraft boundary:

- Maintenance Laptop Port: Ethernet connection for data download and software loading
- Wireless Data Link (ATA 23): Automatic data reporting to ground systems
- USB Ports: Quick Access Recorder data extraction
- Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT): Activation signaling

levelledPara.title: Sensor-to-Display Flow
levelledPara.para: Typical data path from sensor acquisition to cockpit indication:

1. Sensor (e.g., temperature probe) generates analog signal
2. Signal routed to nearest Data Acquisition Unit (DAU)
3. DAU performs A/D conversion, scaling, and validity checks
4. Digital data transmitted via ARINC 429 to IMA module
5. IMA application processes data (averaging, filtering, limit checks)
6. Processed data published on AFDX virtual link
7. Display Management Computer subscribes to AFDX data
8. Display computer renders indication according to ARINC 661 format
9. Rendered display data sent to Display Unit for presentation
Total latency (sensor to display): Typically <100 ms for non-critical parameters

levelledPara.title: Alert Generation and Presentation Flow
levelledPara.para: Alert processing from fault detection to crew notification:

1. Fault condition detected by monitored system (e.g., hydraulic pressure low)
2. System publishes fault message on AFDX network
3. Crew Alerting Computer subscribes to all system fault messages
4. Alert logic applies priority, filtering, and suppression rules
5. Active alerts compiled into prioritized list
6. Alert messages sent to Display Management Computer via AFDX
7. Visual alerts displayed on CAS/ECAM/EICAS display page
8. Master warning/caution lights illuminated (discrete outputs)
9. Aural warning triggered if applicable (audio synthesis)
Total latency (fault to alert): Typically <50 ms for critical warnings

levelledPara.title: Recording Data Flow
levelledPara.para: Flight data path to crash-protected recorders:

1. Parameters acquired from all aircraft systems via AFDX and ARINC 429
2. Data aggregated at Flight Data Acquisition Unit (FDAU)
3. FDAU performs encoding per ED-112A requirements
4. Encoded frame transmitted to Flight Data Recorder (FDR)
5. FDR stores data in crash-protected solid-state memory
6. Parallel data stream sent to Quick Access Recorder (QAR)
7. QAR stores data in removable memory module for ground analysis
8. ACMS Gateway archives subset of data for maintenance and DPP
Recording rate: Typically 1-64 Hz depending on parameter criticality

levelledPara.title: Redundancy and Fault Tolerance
levelledPara.para: The system architecture incorporates multiple levels of redundancy:

- Dual Display Management Computers with automatic failover
- Dual Crew Alerting Computers with cross-monitoring
- Redundant AFDX networks (A and B sides)
- Multiple Data Acquisition Units with overlapping coverage
- Display units capable of presenting combined PFD/ND information if one fails
- Standby flight instruments as ultimate backup for critical parameters
- Independent power supplies for each redundant channel
